newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end firmer but off day's high.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end firmer but off day's high.

text.p: Singapore stock market ended firmer on Tuesday on the back of Wall Street's overnight rebound but dealers said the upside was capped by caution.
After failing to sustain its high at 2,215.36, the Straits Times Industrials Index ended at 2,209.50, up 12.37 points.
Dealers said activity was stymied amid uncertainty over the sustainability of Wall Street's gains.

"The market will continue to trade sideways. Wall Street will dictate the direction of the Singapore stock market for now," a dealer said. Turnover was light at 90.6 million shares, with gainers outpacing losers by 247 to 99.

The SES electronic index, which ended 3.68 percent up at 90.09, was led by gains in Creative, Acma Ltd and Flextech. These firmed on the back of a strong November U.S. book-to-bill ratio for semiconductors.
Multimedia company Creative led gainers and closed Singapore $1.60 (US$1.14) up at S$13.80 on 531,450 lots.
Blue chips rose on buying by foreign institutions especially the foreign tranches of banks like DBS and UOB, dealers said.

Retailer Ossia, which topped the actives with 4.05 million shares, ended unchanged at S$0.525. CityDev saw 3.8 million shares traded, of which 3.0 were crossed at S$13.00. It ended at S$12.80, down 10 cents.
